examples.derivation: The closed segment joins (-2,-1) to (3,3). Its coordinate projections are domain [-2,3] and range [-1,3], with all four boundaries included.
The decreasing segment excludes (-3,3) and includes (2,-2). Therefore -3<x≤2 and -2≤y<3, giving domain (-3,2] and range [-2,3). The solution shadows preserve these inclusions.
The plotted curve is y=x²-2 for -2<x≤1. Its vertex (0,-2) is included. The excluded left endpoint would give y=2; the other solution of x²-2=2 is x=2, outside the domain. Hence the range is [-2,2).
The non-horizontal, non-vertical line has continuation arrows at both ends. Both coordinate projections are unbounded in both directions, so domain and range are each (-∞,∞).
For y=2-x², x²≥0 gives y≤2, with equality at the included vertex (0,2). Both branches continue downward indefinitely. Domain is (-∞,∞); range is (-∞,2].
The plotted exponential is 2^x, defined and positive for every real x. It approaches zero without reaching it and grows without bound. Domain is (-∞,∞); range is (0,∞).

(a) Squaring is increasing for x>4, so x²>16; the boundary is excluded and the range is (16,∞). (b) On [-2,2], the included vertex gives minimum 0 and both included endpoints give maximum 4. The range is [0,4]. Both sketches and solution shadows agree.
